paper_metadata.title: Quantum Generative Models of Mid-Price Movement in Limit Order Books

experiments.description: Training and evaluation of a quantum hidden Markov model / quantum generative model for directional mid-price movement in LOB data at event time and at 1-second aggregated time, using real market data for AMZN and GOOGL.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Hidden Markov Model (QHMM) / unitary quantum generative model with mid-circuit measurement
algorithm.ansatz: custom quantum circuit with mid-circuit measurement; state-preparation + evolution + measurement segments
algorithm.optimizer: memetic algorithm with evolutionary global search, Metropolis annealing local search, and non-linear parametric optimization
algorithm.convergence_criteria: maximum 300 evolutionary generations or until best fitness exceeds -1e-4

hyperparameters.temperature_schedule: Temperature(t) used in Metropolis local search

algorithm.parameter_initialization: initial parent population drawn uniformly at random from the hypothesis space; steady-state preparation uses maximally mixed state

optimizer_settings.self_adaptation: search distributions and hyperparameters adapted by reinforcement learning

problem_formulation.encoding_details: binary directional mid-price movement y_t in {0,1}; one binary symbol per time step; model learns sequence distributions over binary strings
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize fitness F(Q) = -Delta_{<=n}(D^L || D^Q), where Delta is average empirical variational distance over sequence lengths up to n
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: not specified beyond unitary/circuit structure and measurement map M; no explicit penalty formulation

problem_instance.description: Directional mid-price movement modeling for two real LOB datasets, evaluated at event time and at 1-second aggregation.

preprocessing: compute mid-price from bid and ask
binarize directional movement y_t = 1 if r_t > 0 else 0
aggregate to 1-second intervals by taking the last mid-price in each interval

evaluation_methodology: estimate Hankel rank versus sequence length up to 24 symbols
learn models for event-time and 1-second aggregated data
report variational distance between model and target distributions
report results for both AMZN and GOOGL

classical_preprocessing: empirical estimation of finite distributions from observed binary sequences
classical_postprocessing: compare empirical and model sequence distributions

speedup_claims.conditions: for stochastic process languages representable by an HMM with n states
speedup_claims.caveats: Claim cited from prior work [21]; not newly proven in this paper. It refers to representational parsimony, not runtime speedup.

experiments.description: Low-rank approximation study for the same QHMM-based LOB mid-price model, showing how many sequence lengths can be approximated under a 1% approximation error for 3-qubit and 5-qubit models.

algorithm.variant: Low-rank approximation of Hankel matrix for QHMM model selection

problem_formulation.encoding_details: same binary directional movement sequences as the main experiment; approximation is performed on the Hankel matrix of sequence probabilities
problem_formulation.objective_function: approximate the Hankel matrix H_L by a rank-m truncation H_Lm minimizing variance loss
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: retain only largest singular values; no explicit penalty terms

problem_instance.description: Same AMZN and GOOGL event-time and 1-second aggregated LOB datasets, analyzed for low-rank approximation capacity.

preprocessing: construct Hankel matrices from observed sequence probabilities

evaluation_methodology: compare rank growth versus sequence length
report maximum sequence length approximable under epsilon = 0.01 for 3-qubit and 5-qubit models

classical_preprocessing: singular value decomposition of Hankel matrices
compute variance approximation error from singular values
classical_postprocessing: determine maximum sequence length approximable under target error

experiments.description: Hardware execution of trained QHMM circuits for AMZN and GOOGL on IBM Eagle r3 QPU, using 3 time steps and error mitigation.

algorithm.variant: trained unitary QHMM circuits executed on hardware
algorithm.ansatz: custom trained circuit with initial state preparation, evolution unitary, and measurement repeated per time step

problem_formulation.encoding_details: binary sequence generation for 3-symbol outputs from the trained QHMM circuits
problem_formulation.objective_function: generate 3-symbol sequence distributions matching target LOB distributions
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: hardware transpilation to native gate set and layout constraints

problem_instance.description: Hardware validation of trained AMZN and GOOGL QHMM circuits for 3-symbol sequence distributions.

preprocessing: use trained circuits from the earlier QHMM learning stage

evaluation_methodology: run on IBM Eagle r3 QPU
compare hardware output histograms to target distributions for 3-symbol sequences

noise_model.noise_description: real hardware noise; error mitigation applied

classical_preprocessing: transpile circuits to native gate sets
classical_postprocessing: compare hardware histograms with target distributions
